utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-05-88/2-A, The Prosecutor versus Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me make sure first that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Tolimir, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? Mr. Tolimir, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I can hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Counsel for the Prosecution. No problems with the video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Appearances for the parties. The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILANINIA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Nema Milaninia for the Prosecution, joined here with Mr. Todd Schneider and our Case Manager, Ms. Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milaninia. Now, Mr. Tolimir, we do note that you are self-representing. Mr. Aleksandar Gajic, your legal advisor, has a right of audience which is limited to addressing legal or administrative issues during this Status Conference. Mr. Gajic, I see you there. Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes: First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 24 June 2014. Thus, this Status Conference is taking place before the expiration of the 120-day period specified in Rule 65 bis (B). Today's Status Conference was scheduled by the Scheduling Order issued on 12 September 2014. Let me now turn to Mr. Tolimir and inquire into his state of health. If you wish, Mr. Tolimir, I can close the session. Mr. Tolimir. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. God help all of you. My health condition remains unchanged. Therefore, I have nothing to say in that regard, and consequently there's no need for a closed session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. I would like now to update the case. An appeal hearing in this case has been scheduled for Wednesday, 12 November 2014, pursuant to the Scheduling Order of 15 October 2014. The timetable for the appeal hearing is also set out in the Scheduling Order for the appeal hearing. I would also like to recall the Appeals Chamber's decision of 20 June 2014, which authorised Mr. Gajic, Mr. Tolimir's legal advisor, to make oral submissions at the appeal hearing. I would now like to ask the parties whether they would like to raise any issues at this time. Any issues that the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, the Prosecutor. Mr. Tolimir, any issues that you would like to raise? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Since there are no other matters to be raised, I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close.
